standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the higher homotopy groups of the fixed point sets of B Pi
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 1114-1117 and 1134-1135
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes every attaching map of a higher cell contractible in the relevant fixed point set, which is what allows the extension over the skeleta.

core_obligations: Define the map on the 0-skeleton by transporting the value of the natural transformation at the trivial object (proof lines 1081-1082).

Define it on the 1-skeleton: for a G-cell G/H x [0,1] pick the ordinary cell in the H-fixed points, orient it, and let the image be a representative of the element prescribed by the natural transformation; naturality makes the construction independent of the choice of base cell up to homotopy (proof lines 1083-1096).

Extend over the 2-skeleton: the attaching map of the corresponding ordinary 2-cell is contractible in the fixed point set, hence a unit in the fundamental groupoid, and since the transformation is a map of groupoids its image is a unit too, so the map extends over the cell and then equivariantly (proof lines 1098-1112).

Extend over all skeleta and match the induced map: contractibility of the attaching maps from the vanishing of the higher homotopy groups gives the induction, and phi_# = Phi holds because the morphism sets of the groupoid are generated by 1-cells (proof lines 1114-1122).

Uniqueness: any two equivariant maps inducing the same transformation agree on the 0-skeleton and are then joined by an equivariant homotopy built inductively over the skeleta, using phi'_# = phi_# on the 1-skeleton and the vanishing of higher homotopy groups further up (proof lines 1124-1135).
proof_roadmap: Construct the map skeletally: 0-cells from the transformation, 1-cells through fixed point sets and naturality, higher cells by contractibility of attaching maps (proof lines 1081-1117).
Check the induced transformation and prove uniqueness of the map up to equivariant homotopy by the same skeletal induction (proof lines 1119-1135).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states the universal property of the classifying space B Pi of the equivariant fundamental groupoid: for every G-CW-complex Y and every natural transformation Phi from Pi_1(Y;G) to Pi there is a G-equivariant cellular map Y -> B Pi inducing Phi, unique up to G-equivariant homotopy (statement lines 1070-1077). The proof constructs the map skeleton by skeleton, choosing for each G-cell the ordinary cell inside the fixed point set of its isotropy group and prescribing the image through the transformation, and it extends over higher cells because the attaching maps become contractible through the vanishing of the higher homotopy groups of the fixed point sets (proof lines 1081-1117). The step that carries the content is the equivariant extension: the construction has to be checked to be independent of the chosen base cell, which uses naturality, and the extension over each cell uses both the groupoid structure of the transformation and the homotopy vanishing. Uniqueness is then the same induction for a homotopy between two maps. H2.
